title: Guided cost-aware slate — ideation and rough PRD
body:
Context / quick note:
This is a personal scratchpad for an idea: a small, inline UI element I’m calling a ‘guided slate’ that surfaces cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs for model responses and lets product teams (and end users when appropriate) pick a preset. Think of it like a small set of curated response profiles that are annotated with expected token costs and latency percentiles, plus a short rationale.

Why?
- We repeatedly see customers struggle to balance cost vs quality in conversational flows. Engineers want conservative defaults but product teams want high-quality outputs.
- Current controls are scattered (batching, model choice, quantization, max tokens) — developers either hard-code or expose raw knobs to end users.
- A lightweight preset UI could reduce support noise and make deliberate tradeoffs explicit to users.

Hypothesis:
If we provide a small, context-aware slate of 3–4 presets with clear cost/latency/quality annotations and a quick preview, teams will: (a) change fewer configuration files; (b) reduce median per-session token spend 10–25% on non-critical flows; (c) decrease support questions about cost regressions.

Goals (MVP):
- Build a tiny server-side API + client widget that returns 3 presets (economy, balanced, fidelity) for a given route/model + prompt profile.
- Each preset: human label, short blurb about when to use, estimated per-response token cost range, latency p50/p95, and an example response delta (short compare).
- Admins/devs can edit slate per-route in Console (UI to customize labels/estimates).
- Basic telemetry: preset selection rates, effect on tokens/latency, rollback events.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Adoption: 15% of routes with >1k daily requests enabled slate feature.
- Economics: average tokens-per-session drops 8–12% on routes that enable economy preset by default.
- Product: 30% reduction in support tickets about unexpected cost spikes for participating customers.
- UX: 60% click-through on slate suggestions when shown on the Console prototype.

User stories (rough):
1) As a Product Manager I want a curated set of response profiles for the chat route so I can recommend defaults to my UX team and control unit economics without code deploys.
2) As an Engineer I want an API to fetch the slate for any route so I can embed the widget in the client and server-side render the default choice.
3) As an Admin I want to edit labels and override estimated costs for my tenancy so internal accounting matches reality.
4) As an End User (optional) I want a simple toggle like ‘save tokens’ vs ‘best answer’ to pick fidelity without seeing complex settings.

Proposed UX (client widget):
- Compact horizontal card with 3 micro-tiles: Economy | Balanced | Fidelity
- Each tile shows: label, short one-line blurb, tokens estimate (~5–20 token range), p50 latency estimate, small textual example (1–2 lines) — and a radio/select.
- Hover/expand shows a 2-line diff example: economy response vs fidelity quick read.
- Affirmation toast: show expected monthly cost delta if switched. (opt-in)

API surface (sketch):
- GET /v1/slates?route=chat-quick&context_profile=zero-shot -> returns list of presets (id, label, blurb, est_tokens_per_resp, est_p50_ms, est_p95_ms, example_small)
- POST /v1/slates/{route} (console-only) to set overrides
- Telemetry events: slate_shown, slate_selected, slate_previewed, slate_overridden

Server-side considerations:
- Slate generator: initial implementation = rules + heuristics mapping (route, model_family, average prompt length) -> preset numbers.
- Longer-term: use historical telemetry / small regressions to tune estimates per-tenant (privacy guarded, opt-in).
- Backwards compatibility: if no slate configured, API returns null -> widget hides gracefully.

Instrumentation / telemetry needs:
- Track actual tokens/latency for requests tagged with a preset id; compute delta vs baseline.
- Add a single boolean column to request events: slate_preset_id (nullable).
- Console analytics: show per-tenant heatmaps of selections and cost impact.

Rollout plan (MVP):
1) Internal prototype on a handful of non-sensitive routes (docs bot, search assistant).
2) Expose as Console opt-in feature for early adopters; include a small tutorial.
3) Beta to selected customers with an A/B test comparing slate default vs no-slate.

Experiments to run:
- Economy default vs Balanced default: measure tokens/session and NPS (customer survey).
- Context-aware slate (estimates computed using recent 7d telemetry) vs static heuristics.
- End-user exposure vs admin-only control — measure confusion/support.

Open questions / risks (brain dump):
- Accuracy of estimated tokens: customers will distrust wrong numbers. Need conservative bands and clear language (‘estimated’).
- Regulatory/data sensitivity: do not compute tenant-specific examples using customer data unless opt-in. Example snippets must be synthetic or anonymized.
- Gamification / perverse incentives: if users see 'save tokens', they might under-specify prompts and send more back-and-forth, increasing total tokens. Need to measure end-to-end.
- Model-specific behavior: some models degrade gracefully with less context; others hallucinate. Slate needs to warn about quality tradeoffs.

Dependencies:
- Console: small editor panel for slate overrides (UI work).
- Telemetry: minor event tagging and dashboarding in Observability.
- Serving runtime: tagging requests with preset id and returning small preview diffs when requested.

Next steps (my TODO list):
- [ ] Quick Figma mockup for widget (Evan help offered)
- [ ] Prototype API and return static presets for 2 routes (developer-demo by end of week)
- [ ] Create Jira ticket INF-6721 to track implementation tasks (already linked but stub)
- [ ] Write brief customer-facing one-pager for beta customers (tone: transparency + guidance)

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could integrate with Optimize recommendations: when Optimize suggests quantization, also suggest a slate with 'quantized-economy' preset that calls out quality caveats.
- Consider a ‘micro-preview’ where client requests 1 low-cost sample from fidelity preset for visual comparison (cost accounted).
- Might be useful for embeddings workflows too: presets for vector granularity vs price.

End of scratchpad.
(Will iterate; keeping this lightweight so design/eng can riff quickly.)
